Q: How to replace all newlines with paragraph marks in LibreOffice Write A:

I've been looking for this for a couple of weeks now. For whatever reason I did a lot of finding and replacing of paragraph marks in Word, and needed to find the equivalent in LO. I just tried it, also on Mint, same version of LibreOffice and it did work. Be sure to follow the instructions exactly, in particular, be sure you actually select and copy the paragraph mark. Then after you find-all the newlines (\n) be sure to close the search/replace dialog box. You do NOT want to paste the paragraph mark in the Replace box and proceed that way. This might feel counter-intuitive, but go with it. Close the dialog. All the newlines should still be selected from your find-all. Do your Ctrl-v, and it should work.

Q: What is the best approach towards updating a very old MediaWiki installation? A:

I have upgraded a handful of MediaWikis; in the most recent case, from 1.15.3 to 1.43.3.

(Yes, these cases all follow the standard pattern:

  • Someone wants a wiki with certain features
  • Someone else says: I can build that for you, and does
  • Nobody ever thinks of maintenance
  • 15 years later, the wiki breaks, or security comes knocking, and IT support is called.

We're working on that. But anyway.)

I've run into the following caveats:

  • Different MediaWiki versions require different (ranges of) PHP versions.
  • Upgrading MediaWiki involves upgrading the database, which may cause it to be incompatible with the previous MediaWiki, so back up both LocalSettings.php the database if you want to be able to undo an upgrade.
  • Upgrading MediaWiki itself is smooth, but upgrading extensions can be hard or impossible: extensions can be discontinued, forked, renamed, or go through compatibility breaking changes. For instance, we use PluggableAuth with SimpleSAMLphp and the code to configure them in LocalSettings.php had to be rewritten completely. It's not a lot of code, but the logic is nontrivial.
  • People have no qualms about adding / modifying the PHP code. Those changes are even harder to upgrade than extensions. I just drop them - I get paid to do IT support, not development.

My procedure for upgrading MediaWiki is as follows:

  • Reinstall a fresh copy and migrate to it:
    • Open https://releases.wikimedia.org/mediawiki/
    • Determine the existing wiki's version:
      • by opening the Special:Version page in the wiki, or
      • in the code, with grep -r '$wgVersion =' for old versions, or grep -r 'define.*MW_VERSION' for newer ones.
    • Download the tarball or zipfile for that exact version from the right subdirectory of the above URL. Not for mediawiki-core, but for the full mediawiki.
    • Unpack it into a directory on the webserver you can set the document root to.
    • Run a diff -r between the existing wiki and this new directory.
    • Note all differences:
      • added nonstandard extensions in extension/
      • added themes
      • any local code modifications if those exist, save the result of a diff -urd to record them
    • any other custom additions or changes
    • Decide what to do with them. Extensions and themes that are currently supported may be maintained, the rest must go.
    • Prepare the bare directory for hosting the wiki. With my latest upgrade, I did this by creating and running a script ../install-wiki-here with contents as shown below.
    • Edit LocalSettings.php as necessary:
      • Disable all extensions and skins that do not come with MediaWiki. (This varies with the version.)
      • Change the site's document root to this new directory.
      • Make sure the Admin account exists and you know its password (which I create with pwgen -s1 20): php maintenance/createAndPromote.php --sysop Admin <password>
    • Test the site. It should still look and work as before, except that local modifications are no longer in effect and the disabled extensions do not work. Perhaps you need to change the skin to a supported one.
    • Back up the database.
    • Upgrade to the next LTS version:
      • Determine the next LTS version. They are: 1.23, 1.27, 1.31, 1.35, 1.39, 1.43, ...
      • Download its latest minor version from https://releases.wikimedia.org/mediawiki/.
      • Unpack it into a directory on the webserver you can set the document root to.
      • cd to it and run ../install-wiki-here.
      • Run php maintenance/update.php with a compatible version of php.
      • Change the document root to this new directory.
      • Test the site with the same version of PHP.
      • Fix everything in LocalSettings.php that needs to be updated for the new version.
      • Repeat until you're running the wiki on the latest LTS release.
      • Install and enable all extensions that were in use, do not come with MediaWiki, and are still supported by their makers. Using a fork is OK if it is maintained (e.g. as of the time of writing, for EmbedPDF and EmbedVideo.)
    • Test the site again. Ideally, test all extensions.

../install-wiki-here looks like this:

#!/bin/sh

orig=../httpdocs  # or whatever it is in your case

Die() { echo "$@" 1>&2; exit 1; }

[ -f $orig/LocalSettings.php ] || Die cannot find original directory
[ `basename $orig` = `basename $PWD` ] && Die you are in the original directory

set -x

cp -p `ls -t ../*/LocalSettings.php | head -1` $orig/.htaccess .

rm -rf images
ln -s $orig/images .

for d in $orig/extensions/*
do
  if [ -d $d -a ! -d extensions/`basename $d` ]
  then
    ln -s ../$d extensions/
  fi
done

Q: Please create a master key in the database or open the master key in the session before performing this operation A:

I managed to fix this problem once and for all,
by making all of the AG nodes' Server Master Keys (SMKs) the same.

Easiest way to do this is to:

  1. Ensure all your AG nodes' SQL Services are running under the same Windows account (AD User, gMSA, or Service Account)
  2. Backup the Primary node's SMK to a file (we will use this to restore the Secondary nodes' SMKs)
  3. Remove any master-key-encrypted databases from the AG (otherwise your secondary servers will throw errors about data loss, since you are changing how they encrypt their databases)
  4. [Optional] Backup the Secondary nodes' SMKs to files (just for safe-keeping while we do this)
  5. Restore the Secondary nodes' SMKs from the Primary SMK backup file you made.
  6. Add your master-key-encrypted databases back into your AG.

Example Primary AG node code:

USE master
GO
/* useful so you know where you are running, Primary or Secondary? */
SELECT GETDATE() AS [GETDATE]
    ,r.replica_server_name AS ReplicaServer
    ,LEFT(@@VERSION, 52) AS ReplicaVersion
    ,rs.role_desc AS ReplicaRole
    ,rs.connected_state_desc AS ConnectedState
    ,rs.synchronization_health_desc SyncHealth
    ,rs.operational_state_desc AS OperationalState
    ,rs.recovery_health_desc AS RecoveryHealth
    ,SUSER_SNAME(r.owner_sid) AS ReplicaOwner
    ,r.create_date
    ,r.modify_date
    ,r.availability_mode_desc AS AvailabilityMode
    ,r.failover_mode_desc AS FailoverMode
    --,r.seeding_mode_desc AS SeedingMode
    ,r.[session_timeout]
    ,r.primary_role_allow_connections_desc   AS PrimaryRoleAllowConnections
    ,r.secondary_role_allow_connections_desc AS SecondaryRoleAllowConnections
    ,r.[endpoint_url]
    ,r.[read_only_routing_url]
FROM sys.availability_replicas r
JOIN sys.dm_hadr_availability_replica_states rs ON r.replica_id = rs.replica_id
WHERE r.replica_server_name = @@SERVERNAME
GO
/* Create a backup of the service master key. */
BACKUP SERVICE MASTER KEY
TO FILE = 'C:\Temp\service_master_key_YourServerName'
ENCRYPTION BY PASSWORD = 'A strong password here please!'
GO
/*
You can test-restore the file on the AG primary, should get message:

The old and new master keys are identical. No data re-encryption is required.
*/
RESTORE SERVICE MASTER KEY
FROM FILE = 'C:\Temp\service_master_key_YourServerName'
DECRYPTION BY PASSWORD = 'A strong password here please!'
GO
/*
Remove any encrypted databases that are in your AG,
so they disappear from the secondaries.
*/
SELECT d.[name], d.is_master_key_encrypted_by_server
FROM sys.databases d
WHERE d.is_master_key_encrypted_by_server = 1
GO
/*
Add code here to remove the above databases from your AG!

ALTER AVAILABILITY GROUP MyAG REMOVE DATABASE Db6;
*/
GO
/*
Add more code here to add the above databases to your AG later!

ALTER AVAILABILITY GROUP MyAG ADD DATABASE Db6;
*/

Example Secondary AG nodes code:

USE master
GO
/* useful so you know where you are running, Primary or Secondary? */
SELECT GETDATE() AS [GETDATE]
    ,r.replica_server_name AS ReplicaServer
    ,LEFT(@@VERSION, 52) AS ReplicaVersion
    ,rs.role_desc AS ReplicaRole
    ,rs.connected_state_desc AS ConnectedState
    ,rs.synchronization_health_desc SyncHealth
    ,rs.operational_state_desc AS OperationalState
    ,rs.recovery_health_desc AS RecoveryHealth
    ,SUSER_SNAME(r.owner_sid) AS ReplicaOwner
    ,r.create_date
    ,r.modify_date
    ,r.availability_mode_desc AS AvailabilityMode
    ,r.failover_mode_desc AS FailoverMode
    --,r.seeding_mode_desc AS SeedingMode
    ,r.[session_timeout]
    ,r.primary_role_allow_connections_desc   AS PrimaryRoleAllowConnections
    ,r.secondary_role_allow_connections_desc AS SecondaryRoleAllowConnections
    ,r.[endpoint_url]
    ,r.[read_only_routing_url]
FROM sys.availability_replicas r
JOIN sys.dm_hadr_availability_replica_states rs ON r.replica_id = rs.replica_id
WHERE r.replica_server_name = @@SERVERNAME
/*
Try to restore the Primary node's file
onto the secondary nodes!
*/
RESTORE SERVICE MASTER KEY
FROM FILE = '\\NetworkPathToThePrimaryNode\C$\Temp\service_master_key_YourServerName'
DECRYPTION BY PASSWORD = 'A strong password here please!'
GO
/*
If you hit any errors,
check if you still have any encrypted databases:
*/
SELECT d.[name], d.is_master_key_encrypted_by_server
FROM sys.databases d
WHERE d.is_master_key_encrypted_by_server = 1

Useful MS reading:

  • Backup Service Master Key
  • Restore Service Master Key

Q: SQL vs R : when to use which? A:

SQL is good to clean and organize your data, build relationships and make a normalized model of your information. R is good to run statistical analysis on your data, when you would like to discover hidden relationships.

Hint: SQL Server supports R and Python coding from version 2016.

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/machine-learning/tutorials/quickstart-r-create-script?view=sql-server-ver17

Q: Slashes and hashes in Perl and metacharacters A:

There is another depth to this question about escaping forward slashes with the s operator. With my example the capturing becomes the problem.

$image_name =~ s/((http:\/\/.+\/)\/)/$2/g;

For this to work the typo with the addition of a second forward slash, had to be captured. Also, trying to work with just the two slashes did not work. The first slash has to be led by more than one character.

Changing "http://world.com/Photos//space_shots/out_of_this_world.jpg"
To: "http://world.com/Photos/space_shots/out_of_this_world.jpg"
